content: FA2 "convergence" detector does not measure motion. The sum is `Math.abs(attrs.x - Math.round(attrs.x)) + Math.abs(attrs.y - Math.round(attrs.y))` — the fractional part of coordinates, not velocity / displacement. As nodes settle they drift toward integer-ish positions and the fractional part collapses regardless of whether motion stopped, so FA2 will be auto-stopped by this metric even when the layout has not actually relaxed, producing uneven/unconverged visuals. Conversely, a layout stuck at integer offsets will see sum=0 from tick 2 onward and be cut off after 5s. Use `Math.hypot(attrs.x - prevX, attrs.y - prevY)` over real velocity attributes (`vx`/`vy`) instead.
existing_code: sum += Math.abs(attrs.x - Math.round(attrs.x)) + Math.abs(attrs.y - Math.round(attrs.y));

content: wfRunning is set to true when runNow fires a workflow, but there is no listener that resets it to false when the workflow finishes (only sched-status covers jobs, not workflows). As a result the '执行中' badge and the busy-disabled '立即执行' state will persist indefinitely until another event triggers a full reload — and nothing guarantees one. Add a workflow completion event (or schedule a delayed refresh / rely on a single 'workflow-finished' broadcast) to clear wfRunning[targetId]=false, and treat the optimistic set as a hint that must be reconciled.

Silent reload failure produces a misleading empty state. When schedule_overview throws, handleCommandError is called with silent:true and setLoaded(true) is still called, so the UI falls into the '暂无定时任务' branch even though we never successfully fetched — the user is told there are no schedules when in fact we couldn't read them. Track a separate error state (or only set loaded=true on success) and surface a visible error/retry path distinct from 'loaded but truly empty'.

Reset button bypasses `applyBubbleStyle`, so clicking "恢复默认" only updates React local state — the global CSS variables / `data-bubble-bot` attribute are not reset, localStorage is not updated, and no `storage` event fires. Other windows (主窗/挂件) keep the old style until something else changes it. Mirror the `update()` pattern and route the reset through `applyBubbleStyle` (e.g. `setStyle((prev) => applyBubbleStyle({ ...prev, ...resetBubbleStyle() }))` or have `resetBubbleStyle()` itself apply).

            className="nm-outset shrink-0 rounded-[var(--r-sm)] px-3 py-1 text-xs text-[var(--t3)]"
            onClick={() => update(resetBubbleStyle())}
          >
            恢复默认

content: `useEffect` ignores the unsubscribe function returned by `subscribeBubbleStyle`. The "subscribe" naming convention implies it returns a teardown (storage/window listener). Not returning it leaks a listener on every mount/unmount, and any captured closures keep the old component alive. Return the result of `subscribeBubbleStyle` from the effect.

content: Mount-only fetch leaves workflow data stale: `workflow_list` is requested exactly once with no listener for workflow changes (unlike `tasks-changed` which refreshes people). If the user adds/edits/deletes a workflow while GraphPage stays mounted, hub counts, filter options, and graph metadata silently drift out of date. Additionally, both `invoke('workflow_list')` and `loadPeople()` only `console.error` on failure — violating the project's "async errors must surface user-friendly messages" rule (users have no way to tell the hub list is incomplete or retry).

People refresh race: every `tasks-changed` event launches a fresh `loadPeople()` with no cancellation token or response-order guard. Rapid successive events (e.g. bulk import) can resolve out of order, so an older snapshot overwrites a newer `people` array — mis-coloring members, breaking the owner/key palette, and producing flicker. The effect itself has no unmount guard either; if the page unmounts while a load is in flight, `setPeople` fires on an unmounted component.

Dependency writes are snapshot-based and fire-and-forget: `addDependency`/`removeDependency` derive the new `dependsOn` from `selectedNode?.task` (a closed-over render snapshot) and call the void `onPatchTask` without awaiting/rollback/error surface. Fast successive clicks or parent-side asynchronous patch handling let the second click overwrite the first's payload, silently dropping a dependency; a rejected `task_patch` never surfaces to the user and the editor stays out of sync with backend state. There is also no use of the functional setter form, so multiple queued writes within one render batch all read the same stale `dependsOn`.

Inline-vs-block detection via position line count is unreliable. CommonMark allows code spans to contain line endings (normalized to spaces), so a multi-line `` `https://...\nfoo` `` inline code span will be classified as a block (isBlock=true) and skip linkification. Conversely, a one-line 4-space indented code block has start.line === end.line and will be treated as inline — if its text is a URL or path, openTarget will be invoked on content that was never meant to be a link. The comment "inline code doesn't span lines" is factually wrong per the CommonMark spec. Consider using `node.tagName` (via the `inline`/`block` distinction from remark) or checking the parent node type instead.

Inline-code linkification bypasses react-markdown's normal URL sanitization pipeline. The rendered `<code>` text is routed straight to `openTarget` via `isHttpUrl`/`isAbsPath` helpers — any model output that happens to be a string recognized by those helpers (e.g. `https://...`, `/etc/passwd`, `\\server\share`, possibly `//evil.com` depending on the helper) becomes a clickable action. Because this is untrusted assistant text, confirm that `isHttpUrl` strictly rejects non-http(s) schemes (javascript:, data:, file:, vbscript:) and that `isAbsPath` does not match UNC, protocol-relative URLs, or other ambiguous forms that could escape to an unintended handler in `openTarget`. Also consider whether remote Markdown images should be allowed — there is no `img` override, so arbitrary image URLs from the model will trigger browser requests (privacy/tracking).

`openTarget` is invoked without observing its result. `e.preventDefault()` has already suppressed the native navigation, so if `openTarget` returns a rejected promise or throws, the user sees a dead link with no browser fallback. Even if `openTarget` is expected to surface failures via a popup (per the file-level comment), this contract is not enforced anywhere in this file. Wrap `activate()` in a try/catch (or `.catch(...)` if async) that re-enables native navigation or surfaces an error, so a transient backend failure doesn't silently break clicking.

Nested ternary expression violates the project's "no nested ternary" rule. `src ? <img...> : kind === "bot" ? <img...> : <span...>` is a nested conditional embedded in JSX. Extract to a small helper component (e.g., `<ProfileAvatar entry={entry} fallbackSrc={botLogo} label={label} />`) or compute the element via an if/early-return inside a helper so JSX only renders one branch.
suggestion_code: ... function ProfileAvatar({ entry, kind, fallbackSrc, label, }: { entry: { name: string; avatarDataUrl?: string } | null; kind: "user" | "bot"; fallbackSrc: string; label: string; }) { const displayName = entry?.name ?? ""; if (entry?.avatarDataUrl) { return ; } if (kind === "bot") { return ; } return {displayName.charAt(0)}; }

content: The `useEffect` already requires `oxlint-disable react/set-state-in-effect` to silence the linter, and `runTest` is an unawaited async invoke with no cancellation. If the user edits `model.baseUrl` (or `apiProvider`) while a probe is in flight, the effect resets state to `"idle"`/`""`, but the in-flight `invoke` will eventually resolve and overwrite that with `"ok"`/green for a URL the user has already changed — leaving the row displaying a stale "连接成功" badge for an outdated endpoint. Guard the late resolve with a stale-check (token / ref counter) or use AbortController-style cancellation.

SSRF: HTTP transport URL is not validated despite the UI promise of "仅公网地址". `buildPayload` only checks the URL is non-empty — nothing rejects `file://`, `http://127.0.0.1`, `http://169.254.169.254` (cloud metadata), or RFC1918 private ranges. Because the bot later invokes the tool layer against whatever URL is stored, a malicious or accidental entry can be used to probe internal services or read cloud metadata. Add a scheme allowlist (http/https only), parse the host, and reject loopback / link-local / private ranges (or at least surface a hard validation error rather than just a placeholder hint).

`saveEdit` / `removeItem` clear `editingId` / proceed to reload right after the IPC succeeds, but the subsequent `await reload(...)` follows `reload`'s own catch path (which only sets `loadError`, not `rowError`). If the write succeeded but the refresh failed, the user sees the top `loadError` and stale rows with no indication their edit/delete actually persisted server-side. Surface a `rowError` after `reload()` (or roll back the optimistic clear) so the failure mode is visible in the row context.

`diff.split("\n")` will throw if the parent passes `undefined`/`null` for the `diff` prop (TypeScript only enforces the type when the caller is also typed). Since this component is fed from external data, add a guard at the boundary (e.g., default to `""`, or render a fallback) to avoid a runtime crash.

content: Trashed cards can still enter title edit on click. The onClick handler only checks `archived`, not `trashed`, and the effect that resets `editing` only fires when the prop changes — so a user click on a trashed title sets `editing=true`, an input renders, and the next blur commits the change, bypassing the read-only intent. Guard the click on both flags.

The effect only resets `editing` when `archived`/`trashed` become true. If a bot / auto-archive / external mutation flips the task to read-only while note/tag/subtask/due-date editors are already open, those inputs stay mounted and blur/Enter still commit changes, violating the read-only contract. Reset every transient editor state on the same transition.

`handleCommandError` already raises a user-facing error dialog (in-app or fallback alert). The extra `alert(...)` call afterwards produces a second notification with the same content (and a weaker message via `formatCommandError`). Remove the manual `alert`; if a follow-up hint is required, pass it through the error-handling channel.

`React.PointerEvent` is referenced but `React` is never imported (`import { useEffect, useState } from "react"`). Under the project's `jsx: react-jsx` setting the global `React` namespace is not auto-available, so this will fail type-checking or silently rely on ambient types. Import the type explicitly or change the signature to `PointerEvent`.

content: `sumByKey` accumulates every row in `rows` regardless of whether the row's `day` falls inside the current `trendDays` window that the caller passes as `days`. Because `modelDays` state is replaced only when a range-specific fetch resolves, the period between switching the range and the new fetch landing uses the previous window's rows — so top-N ranking (and thus the visible series) is decided by stale data, and models with no activity in the new window can show up as flat-zero lines while current-window models are dropped. Gate the sum on the same `i !== undefined` check used for the per-day slot (or filter `rows` to `days` up-front).

Functional bug: once a question is opened for editing it can never collapse back to the summary row, contradicting the documented "已答卡折叠为摘要行可重开编辑" behavior. `onToggleEdit` only ever sets `editing[q.id] = true`, and `collapsed` requires `!editing[q.id]`. So after the user clicks the pencil on an answered row, that row stays expanded for the rest of the session even if they then type a fresh answer, change a chip, or clear it via the X button (which also forgets to reset `editing`). The pencil button needs a "done / collapse" path, or `collapsed` should be recomputed from a single derived flag rather than a one-way latch.

Accessibility conflict on the X "clear answer" control. The element carries both `aria-hidden` (which hides it from assistive tech) and `role="button"` + `aria-label="清除回答"` + an onClick handler. Screen readers will either ignore the control or announce it inconsistently. For an interactive SVG you should drop `aria-hidden`; the parent span already has the visual "已回答" label so consider using a real <button> instead of a clickable SVG.

content: `React.memo` wrapping is likely ineffective: `GoalNode` receives the entire `data` object (including `onRename`/`onGoalChange` callbacks) as a single prop, and React Flow re-renders the canvas frequently. If the parent constructs a new `data` object per render (typical for node updates), memo shallow-compares a new reference every time and never short-circuits. To make memo useful, either (a) have the parent memoize `data` and stabilize the callbacks with `useCallback`, or (b) accept only the primitive fields the node actually needs and hoist callbacks into the node via `useReactFlow().setNodes` instead of prop drilling.

content: Hidden `Handle` contradicts the "不参与连线" contract. The header comment says this node "doesn't participate in connections", yet a target `Handle` is still rendered with `!opacity-0`. React Flow hit-testing operates on the handle regardless of opacity, so connections may still be attempted/dropped here. Either drop the `Handle` entirely (and remove the dependency on it), or document why it must stay hidden-but-active for layout/z-index reasons.

content: Re-entrancy hazard: if a second pointerdown fires before the first drag's pointerup (or before its async `startPos` resolves), every call stacks another set of pointermove/up/cancel listeners on `window` while only overwriting `dragCleanupRef.current`. The previous listeners and its `cleanup` closure become orphaned (never removed), pointer capture on the first `el` is never released, and `setWidgetDragActive` is a non-balanced boolean — when the first drag's cleanup finally runs it flips the global flag to `false` even though the second drag is still active, breaking the drag-active invariant downstream. Guard the start of `onDown` by checking `dragCleanupRef.current` (or a "dragging" ref) and call/clear the previous cleanup before registering new listeners; also make `setWidgetDragActive` reference-counted.

Drag-guard reset is not tracked or cleaned up. The zero-delay `setTimeout` handle is discarded, so an in-flight timer from a previous drag can still fire after a new drag has started (e.g., rapid drag-then-drag, or a `task.id` change while a reset is pending) and flip `wasDragging.current` back to `false` mid-drag, causing the next click to incorrectly trigger `onSelect`. Store the handle and cancel it on `onDragStart` and on unmount/effect cleanup (e.g., a `useEffect` that clears the pending timer when `task.id` changes or the component unmounts).

Card-level click handler does not exclude bubbled events from child interactive controls. The comment states the wrapper should select on plain card clicks but exclude "internal interaction buttons"; however, this handler runs for every click that bubbles up, so toggling done/collapse, editing the title, opening/copying/removing a file, or triggering the bot action will also call `onSelect`. Filter by `event.target === event.currentTarget` here (and/or require `TaskCardContent` to stop propagation on its controls), so selection only fires on truly empty-card clicks.

Unsafe type cast on `e.target`: `e.target` can be `null` or a non-`Element` in TypeScript's React types. Calling `.closest("button")` on a null/undefined cast will throw at runtime. Add a null/Element guard or use `(e.target as Element | null)?.closest(...)`.

Also `e.currentTarget as HTMLElement` on the next line is similarly unchecked — though React guarantees it for the bound handler, the same DOM node is captured into `el` and later used in `releasePointerCapture` after the component may have unmounted.

Icon-only buttons lack `aria-label`. The `title` attribute is not a reliable accessible name across browsers/screen readers. Add explicit `aria-label="聊天区变大"` / `aria-label="任务区变大"` (and prefer translations strings if i18n is used elsewhere). Also consider `type="button"` to prevent any accidental form submission if this component is ever rendered inside a form.

content:
Touch devices need `touch-action: none` (or `touch-action: pan-y`) on the drag handle. Without it, a vertical drag on touch will scroll the page instead of resizing, breaking the whole feature for mobile/tablet users. Add `touch-action-none` (Tailwind) or `style={{ touchAction: 'none' }}` on the outer `div`.

Additionally, `e.stopPropagation()` on pointerdown runs before knowing whether a drag will actually start — even for a 0-pixel nudge this swallows the event from any parent gesture handler. Consider only calling `stopPropagation` once a non-trivial movement is detected in `move`.

      onPointerDown={onDown}
    >

content: Render-phase ref write: `expandedRef.current = expanded` is mutated during render (oxlint disabled). This breaks React's render-purity contract and can desync under React 18 concurrent rendering / StrictMode double-invoke, undermining the very "same-tick latest" guarantee the comment claims. Move the assignment into a `useEffect([expanded])` (or use the `useEvent` / `useSyncExternalStore`-style ref pattern) so listeners always read the latest committed value without leaning on a render-side mutation.

Stale closure in `expandFnRef` / no-deps effect pattern: `expandFnRef.current = expand` runs after every render, but `expand` closes over React state (`size.w`/`size.h`/`botOn`). Between a resize commit (e.g. user drags a resize edge) and the next effect flush, `chat-focus-session` will dispatch the previous `expand` with the previous `size`, producing an incorrect window width. Mirror `size`/`botOn` into refs and read them inside `expand`, or memoize `expand` against `size`/`botOn` and refresh the ref via a `[size, botOn]`-keyed effect.

armedTimerRef is shared between this `deleteWorkflow` two-step confirm and `regenerate()`'s two-step confirm. If the user arms delete (timer T1 set), then within 3s clicks 重新生成, regenerate's `clearTimeout(armedTimerRef.current)` wipes T1, so the `setDeleteArmed(false)` reset never fires — `deleteArmed` stays true indefinitely. The toolbar then permanently shows '确认删除？' and a single click deletes the workflow. Use two separate timer refs (one per armed flag) and reset the *other* flag when entering either confirm flow.

Same root cause as the deleteWorkflow issue: this two-step confirm reuses armedTimerRef, so arming regenerate within 3s of delete (or vice versa) silently cancels the other side's auto-reset. The earlier armed flag (deleteArmed or regenArmed) stays `true` until something else resets it, leaving a destructive one-click window. Use independent timer refs and explicitly reset the *other* armed flag when entering either confirm flow.

createBlank resets wfReport / lastAnswers / assumptions / running but does NOT clear `nodeLive`. Neither does openWorkflow. Stale `liveStatus` entries from previously-rendered workflows persist and are merged into the new canvas via rfNodes. Combined with the `workflow-node-status` listener not filtering by workflowId, switching canvases can render wrong run-state highlights on reused task IDs and pollutes the cache across runs. Add `setNodeLive({});` here and in openWorkflow alongside `setWfReport(null)`.

This listener accepts `workflow-node-status` events from any workflow — the payload type has no `workflowId` field and the callback never filters. Compare with the `workflow-report` listener below, which correctly gates on `activeIdRef.current`. As a result, a backgrounded/older workflow's run events keep updating `nodeLive` for the active canvas. Have the backend emit `workflowId` and filter here, otherwise cross-workflow contamination is inevitable.

finish() captures `req` from the render that produced the buttons, but the file's own comment says `reqRef` is a synchronous mirror specifically to "新请求顶掉旧请求前先把旧的 resolve(false)，否则旧调用方的 await 永久悬挂". The handler correctly uses `reqRef.current`, but finish does not — it relies on the state-closure `req`. Race: ERROR_DIALOG_EVENT fires, handler runs `reqRef.current = req2; prev.resolve(false); setReq(req2)`. Before React commits the new state, the user clicks the still-rendered overlay/buttons. The OLD render's finish runs: `req.resolve(false)` (no-op on the already-resolved prev), then `reqRef.current = null` and `setReq(null)`. The newly captured `req2` is now unrecoverable — its `resolve` is never called and its caller's `await` hangs forever. finish must read from `reqRef.current` to stay consistent with the supersede protocol.

Modal a11y is incomplete for `role="alertdialog"`: `aria-modal="true"` is missing, there is no initial focus on the primary button, no focus trap, and no ESC key handler. Keyboard / screen-reader users cannot dismiss the full-screen backdrop (`fixed inset-0`) without aiming at the small Cancel/OK buttons, and focus can leak to the controls behind the overlay while it is shown.

        onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
        role="alertdialog"
        aria-modal="true"
        aria-labelledby="error-dialog-title"
        aria-describedby="error-dialog-message"
        onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === "Escape") finish(false); }}
      >

content: Optimistic state is never reverted on `upsertWorkspaceItems` failure. `setItems(next)` runs before the await, and the `catch` only swallows the rejection. A failed write leaves the UI diverged from the DB until the next reload, and subsequent `persist` calls use the optimistic `items` as their base, compounding the divergence (failed changes get re-saved alongside new ones). Either revert on failure, or roll back via a `setItems((prev) => previous)` snapshot captured before the optimistic update.

Rapid double-clicks on "新建工作区" race against the stale closure of `items`. `persist` calls `setItems(next)` synchronously but React doesn't re-render until the next tick, so a second `addItem()` invoked immediately after the first still reads the pre-update `items` from closure and computes the same `max + 1` order. Both items get the same `order`, and the second `persist([...items, D])` makes the first item C disappear from state (it may or may not survive depending on storage semantics). Compute the new order/max inside the functional updater or inside `persist` itself.

Inconsistent delete confirmation: `remove` uses native `window.confirm` while `SaveConfirmDialog` is a styled in-app modal. `window.confirm` blocks the JS thread, can be suppressed/styled by the Tauri webview host, and breaks the auditability standard the rest of the panel enforces (save path explicitly exposes the argv/headers before persistence). Replace with a dialog matching `SaveConfirmDialog`, or reuse the same component pattern.
